stem: The new queuing system has shortened the waiting time at the cashier. ___, many clients still complain, because the line now forms outside the building under the hot sun.
hints: Is the first sentence good news or bad news? What about the second?
The word 'still' in the second sentence is a clue. It means 'even so'.
Name the link between a good result and a complaint, then pick the connector for that link.

solution.methodName: Name the link, then pick the connector

steps.action: Read the first sentence: good news. The waiting time is shorter.
Read the second sentence: bad news. Many clients still complain.
Spot the clue 'still': the complaints continue even after the improvement.
steps.why: 'Still' often signals that something is true in spite of what came before.

steps.action: Name the link: contrast, good news set against bad news.

steps.why: Moreover adds a similar idea, therefore shows a result, and similarly shows that two things are alike. Only however shows contrast.

trapNotes.Moreover: Moreover adds another point of the same kind. But the second sentence is a complaint, not another good thing about the system.
trapNotes.Therefore: Therefore shows a result. A shorter wait does not cause complaints; the complaints are about the line being outside in the sun.
trapNotes.Similarly: Similarly shows that two things are alike. A shorter wait and new complaints are opposites, not alike.
